observations.claim: The maximum node step ratio failed the 80% headroom requirement before any node exhausted the 48-step cap.

Responding peers performed most model processing and repeated chain assembly: four non-entry checkpoint attempts were rejected, and peers created independent requests and assembled full-chain responses.

The historical prompt invites each peer to resolve the shared chain and choose its own role; the tool guard permits only entry checkpoints. This is a workflow coordination ambiguity supported by the rejected attempts.

observations.claim: No persisted rewire or evidence-access failure was observed in this run; all 22 rewires changed topology, committed durably, and had prior successful status queries.

Additional tool calls include 8 invalid board discovery publications, 3 malformed result sends, 3 non-neighbour sends, 2 stale board cursors, and 1 unknown task. These guards rejected misuse rather than silently accepting it.

The endpoint holder response to the entry required a retry for omitted to/kind fields and settled after 58.476 seconds. The observed latency includes concurrent work and model time and cannot be fully attributed to that retry.
About 92% of the known total token count is cache-read input. Repeated turns still consume the observed-total-token admission threshold even when most context is cached.

minimalPromptOnlyWorkflowChange: Assign the host-owned entry responsibility for cross-copy current/stale validation, chain assembly and both checkpoints. A root holder or relay coordinator is still a responding peer.

Responding peers publish their own exact discoveryHints and concise local evidence once per phase, answer actual fact/relay tasks, and wait after settling them. They should not independently re-search the whole chain, broadcast unsolicited chain updates, poll while idle or rewrite unchanged board facts.

Return the exact local copy for a requested key even if phase/version is obsolete. Fetch a replacement only when the task explicitly requests relay to a named holder. Always include the actual requester in to, kind=result, and the actual taskId when returning a result.

recommendations.fixedRingRelayRemainsValid: When an actual relay task targets a non-neighbour holder, responding peers must forward to an unvisited outgoing ring neighbour, preserve original target/key/phase/version and visited nodes, then settle the upstream task with the unchanged exact result. Waiting applies after real work is settled, not while a requested relay is pending; host phase updates and incoming tasks can wake the peer.
